overall: The AG found the Lowell City Council violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to certify receipt of OML materials, declined to review the clerk allegation, declined to find the violation intentional, and ordered certification and future compliance.

allegations.summary: Members of the Lowell City Council allegedly failed to certify receipt of Open Meeting Law materials within two weeks of taking office.
allegations.key_passage: The Council does not dispute that members failed to certify that they received copies of the Open Meeting Law, regulations, and educational material.

allegations.summary: A complainant alleged the City Clerk violated the law by failing to provide materials to members and failing to retain their certifications.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we decline to review any separate allegation that the Lowell City Clerk also violated the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: The complainant alleged the certification violation was intentional, citing prior Open Meeting Law determinations against the Council.
allegations.key_passage: However, neither determination concerned the failure to certify receipt of educational materials.

remedy: Certify within thirty (30) days of receipt of the letter, on the AG-approved form, receipt of the Open Meeting Law, the AG's regulations, and the AG's Open Meeting Law Guide.
Certify to the AG's Office within thirty (30) days of receipt of the letter that the Council has complied with the certification order.
Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that a similar future violation may be considered evidence of an intentional violation.
remedy_passage: We order the Council to certify within thirty (30) days of receipt of this letter, on the form approved by the Office of the Attorney General, that they have received a copy of the Open Meeting Law, the Attorney General’s regulations, and the Attorney General’s Open Meeting Law Guide.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
